p1.original: 关于记忆有一个简单的公式，我们可以用下面的例子来阐释。请花几秒的时间学习这组字母：
p1.en: There is a simple formula for memory, which we can explain by way of example. Please take a few seconds to study this group of letters:

p2.original: I B M U F O F B I L O L
p2.en: I B M U F O F B I L O L

p3.original: 不要偷看下面的解释，请按呈现顺序尽可能多地写出你记住的字母。
p3.en: Do not peek at the explanations below, write as many letters as you can remember in the order in which they are presented.

p4.original: 大多数人能准确记住5到7个字母。少数人能记住全部字母，他们是如何做到的呢？他们找到了一个规律（你可能注意到了上面的字母中有一些熟悉的缩写：IBM，UFO，FBI，LOL）。找到规律就会大大简化记忆任务，因为你可以利用已存储在记忆中的材料。在这种情况下，你所需要记住的是四个“组块”信息，而不是12个不相关的字母。
p4.en: Most people remember five to seven letters precisely. How can a few remember the full letter? They found a pattern (you may have noticed some familiar acronyms in the letters: IBM, UFO, FBI, LOL). Finding patterns will greatly simplify memory tasks, because you can use materials stored in memory. In this case, all you need to remember is four “blocks” messages, not 12 unrelated letters.

p5.original: 这个方法也适用于心理学课程的学习材料。如果你试图把每条信息都作为单独的项目来记忆，会觉得比较困难，但是如果你找到规律，你会发现其实学习并不难，而且更加有趣。
p5.en: This approach also applies to learning materials for psychological courses. If you try to remember every information as a separate project, it's more difficult, but if you find a pattern, you find it easy and more interesting to learn.

p6.original: 运用心理学来学习心理学

p7.original: 那么如何来识别这些规律呢？为此我们开发了一些独具特色的学习版块，帮助读者快速掌握相关知识。
p7.en: So how do we identify these patterns? To this end, we have developed special learning sections to help readers quickly acquire relevant knowledge.

p8.original: 核心概念 我们围绕着一个被称为核心概念的重要理念来组织每一章的主要内容。例如，第五章有四个核心概念，其中记忆的核心概念如下：
p8.en: We organize the main elements of each chapter around an important concept called the core concept. For example, chapter V contains four core concepts, of which the core concepts of memory are as follows:

p10.original: 人类的记忆是一种信息加工系统，它会对信息进行建设性的编码、存储和提取。
p10.en: Human memory is an information-processing system that is constructive in coding, storing and extracting information.

p11.original: 因此，我们将核心概念作为中心主题，围绕它组织了大约10页材料（包括几个新术语）。当你阅读每一章的内容时，记住核心概念将帮助你编码与该概念相关的新术语和思想，并将它们存储在你的记忆中，然后在你接受测试时提取它们。正如一句老话所说，核心概念就是“森林”，而章节中的细节就是“树木”。
p11.en: We have therefore organized around the core concept, as the central theme, some 10 pages of material (including several new terms). When you read the contents of each chapter, remember that the core concept will help you to codify new terms and ideas related to the concept and store them in your memory, and then extract them when you are tested. As the old saying goes, the core concept is “forests”, while the details in the chapter are “trees”.

p12.original: 关键问题 每个核心概念都有一个关键问题作为本章的主要标题。例如，下面是记忆一章的关键问题：
p12.en: Each core concept has a key issue as the main title of this chapter. The following are, for example, the key questions of the chapter on memory:

p13.original: 为什么记忆有时会出错，对此我们能做些什么？
p13.en: Why do memories sometimes go wrong, and what can we do about it?

p14.original: 这样一些关键问题将帮助你提前了解本部分中最重要的观点或核心概念。事实上，核心概念总是为关键问题提供一个简短的答案。“关键问题”如同汽车上的远光灯，可以帮助你聚焦前方。我们的“关键问题”也可以作为你对阅读内容提出问题的指南。
p14.en: These key issues will help you to understand in advance the most important points or core concepts in this section. Indeed, the core concept always provides a brief answer to the key questions. The key issues, like the remote light on the car, can help you focus on the front. Our “key issues” can also serve as a guide to your questions about reading content.

p15.original: 另外，核心概念和关键问题随后会作为章节小结的组织特征再次呈现。
p15.en: In addition, core concepts and key issues are subsequently re-emerged as the organizational features of the chapters.

p16.original: 心理学很有用 心理学与新闻事件和日常生活有着许多让人着迷的联系，我们在每一章的各个主要部分的结尾都探索了其中的一种联系。为了说明这一点，下面举几个来自“记忆”一章的例子。
p16.en: Psychology is very useful, and psychology has many fascinating connections to news events and everyday life, one of which we explored at the end of each of the main chapters. To illustrate this point, the following are some examples from the “Memory” chapter.

p17.original: 你想拥有“摄影式记忆”吗？

p18.original: 闪光灯记忆：当……的时候，你在哪儿？
p18.en: Flash memory: Where were you when...?

p20.original: 这种联系非常实用、接地气、引人入胜，它们将帮助你将心理学研究与你的实际生活经验联系起来。它们还将帮助你批判性地评估你在媒体上看到的许多心理学观点，例如，当你看到以“心理学研究表明……”开头的新闻报道时。到本课程结束时，你将成为一个更加理性的信息消费者。其中一些专题特别注重将心理学应用到学习和研究中，因此学生可以获得很多“运用心理学来学习心理学”的实用技巧。
p20.en: This link is very practical, earth-breeding and fascinating, and it will help you to link psychological research to your practical life experience. They will also help you critically to assess many of the psychological views you see in the media, for example, when you see news reports beginning with “psychological studies...”. By the end of this course, you will be a more rational consumer of information. Some of these topics focus particularly on the application of psychology to learning and research, so that students can gain a lot of practical skills in “using psychology to learn psychology”.

p21.original: 试一试 在整本书中，我们安排了很多主动学习的演示，例如，要求你记住字母I B M U F O F B I L O L。除了有趣之外，这些活动还有一个严肃的目的，即阐明文中讨论的重要原则。例如，在第五章中，“试一试”版块可以帮助你发现你的工作记忆容量；另一版块则可以测试你“摄影式记忆”的能力。
p21.en: And in the book as a whole, we've arranged a lot of active learning presentations, for example, to ask you to remember the letters I B M U F F B I L. In addition to being interesting, these activities have a serious purpose, namely, to clarify the important principles discussed in the text. For example, in chapter V, the “tried out” section can help you to discover your work memory capacity; And the other part of it is the ability to test your photo-memory.

p22.original: 关键术语 书中最重要的术语均以粗体显示。在本书最后的术语表中，我们将各章的关键术语和定义进一步集中汇总。
p22.en: Key terms The most important terms in the book are shown in bold. In the glossary at the end of the book, we have further centralized key terms and definitions for each chapter.

p23.original: 本章小结 这部分概述了每一章的主要观点，以帮助你预览和复习该章。但我们要提出一个警告：阅读“本章小结”并不能代替阅读整章！这里还要给出一个有用的提示：我们建议你在阅读本章的其余部分之前先阅读小结，以便对接下来的内容有所了解，然后在读完本章之后再重新阅读小结。先阅读小结可以为你的阅读材料提供一个框架，这样你的阅读材料就可以更容易地编码和存储在你的记忆中。当然，在阅读完一章之后进行复习和总结会巩固你刚刚学到的知识，使你在需要的时候（如考试）能想起它。
p23.en: This chapter summarizes the main points of each chapter to help you preview and review it. But let us warn you that reading this chapter's summary is not a substitute for reading the whole chapter. Here is also a useful reminder: we suggest that you read the summary before reading the rest of this chapter, so that you can understand what follows and then reread the summary after reading this chapter. Reading a knot first can provide a framework for your reading material, so that your reading material can be more easily encoded and stored in your memory. Of course, the review and wrap-up session after reading a chapter consolidates the knowledge you have just learned and brings it to your mind when you need it, such as an examination.

p25.original: 只学习心理学的事实和定义不会让你成为心理学家。除了这些事实之外，如果你想像心理学家一样思考，还需要学习一些解决问题和批判性思维的技巧，这是任何一个优秀的心理学家都应该掌握的。考虑到这个目标，我们为本书添加了两个独特的部分。
p25.en: Learning the facts and definitions of psychology alone does not make you a psychologist. In addition to these facts, if you want to think like a psychologist, you need to learn some problem-solving and critical thinking skills, which any good psychologist should know. With this goal in mind, we have added two distinct parts to the book.

p26.original: 本章思考题 本书每章都以一个重要的问题开始，并且告诉读者，通过阅读你将获得相关的工具来解决这个问题。这些问题大多非常有趣，如测试糖果会不会让孩子“糖亢奋”、如何评估“恢复的记忆”、如何区分“天才”与普通人。
p26.en: This chapter begins with an important question in every chapter of this book and tells readers that you will have the tools to solve this problem by reading it. Most of these questions are very interesting, such as testing whether sweets make children “sugars” — how to assess “recovered memories” and how to distinguish between “genius” and ordinary people.

p27.original: 批判性思维的应用 在每章章末，我们会要求你认真思考心理学家之间争论的问题和媒体上提出的问题，如潜意识的本质和潜意识说服的效果。解决每一个问题都需要你具有怀疑的态度和一套特殊的批判性思维技巧，我们将在第一章中进行介绍。
p27.en: The application of critical thinking at the end of each chapter, we will ask you to think seriously about the issues that are debated between psychologists and those that are raised in the media, such as the nature of subconsciousness and the effect of subconscious persuasion. Addressing each of these issues requires your skepticism and a special set of critical thinking skills, which we will present in chapter I.

p28.original: 最后，我们还有一个帮助你在心理学上取得成功的建议：本书用很多例子来说明最重要的观点，但如果你在学习的时候能够自己生成例子，那么你会把这些观点记得更牢。这个习惯将会使各种信息内化成你自己的知识。因此，我们祝愿大家在我们共同热爱的领域中拥有一次难忘的旅程。
p28.en: Finally, we have a suggestion to help you succeed psychologically: this book offers many examples of the most important points, but if you can produce them yourself when you learn, you will remember them more firmly. This habit will internalize information into your own knowledge. We therefore wish you all an unforgettable journey in the field that we all love.

p31.original: 你熟悉和喜爱的前七版的一些特点都得以保留：关键问题、核心概念、本章思考题、批判性思维的应用，以及多样性分析与跨文化心理学，这些模块的写作引人入胜，每一个概念都有清晰的例子佐证。
p31.en: Some of the features of the first seven editions, which you know and love, are preserved: key issues, core concepts, the subject of reflection in this chapter, the application of critical thinking, and diversity analysis and intercultural psychology, the writing of which is fascinating and each of which is supported by clear examples.

p32.original: 当然，新版本还介绍了心理学领域许多令人兴奋的新发展。例如，飞速发展的表观遗传学及其对发育、健康和精神障碍的意义；开发基于大脑的DSM-5替代品的倡议；班杜拉用于解释不道德行为的“道德推脱”理论；卡罗尔·德韦克关于思维定势的惊人力量的发现。所有这些新材料都与心理学的某一核心概念相联系。
p32.en: Of course, the new version also presents many exciting new developments in the area of psychology. For example, the rapid development of epigenetics and its implications for development, health and mental disorders; Initiatives to develop brain-based alternatives to DSM-5; (a) The doctrine of moral deviance used by Bandura to explain immoral behaviour; Carol Dewey's discovery of the amazing power of the mindset. All these new materials are linked to a core concept of psychology.

p33.en: The core concept of Zimbabwe General Psychology (version 8) is not simply a routine revision or a quick update, but a very important update. We will now turn to the chapter-by-chapter additions to version 8.
